introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, Ordinary Level Examination, June 2020. Chemistry, Paper 2 (subject code 0515). Duration: two and a half hours.

This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: attempt ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 questions answered. Section B: answer BOTH questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3.

In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Organic Compounds can be represented using the following general formula:

- A: $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}$
- B: $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}COOH}$
- C: $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$
- D: $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}$
incertitudes: Question 3(b) et 3(e) : le « premier membre » de B (CnH2n+1COOH) est ambigu. Le corrige retient HCOOH comme premier (n = 0) : 3e membre C2H5COOH, 2e membre CH3COOH, ester = ethanoate de propyle. Si le bareme compte a partir de n = 1, le 3e membre serait C3H7COOH et le 2e C2H5COOH (ester : propanoate de propyle) ; les deux lectures sont notees dans le corrige.

Regle de choix de la Section A : l'en-tete dit « ATTEMPT ALL 5 questions. You will be graded for the best 4 », le titre de la section dit « Answer ALL questions ». Les deux sont compatibles ; la regle est codee « 4 sur 5 » (les 4 meilleures comptent), tous les exercices restant a traiter.
Le filigrane (gcerevision.com) et des annotations manuscrites parasites sont ignores ; les pages portent aussi des traces de transparence (texte inverse du verso), sans effet sur la lecture.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the homologous series to which A and D belong.

A: ...

D: ... *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **A** ($\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}$) belongs to the **alkenes**.
- **D** ($\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}$) belongs to the **alcohols** (alkanols).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the formula of the third member of B and C.

B: ...

C: ... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **B** ($\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}COOH}$, the carboxylic acids): the members are $\mathrm{HCOOH}$ ($n=0$), $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ ($n=1$) and $\mathrm{C_2H_5COOH}$ ($n=2$). The third member is **$\mathrm{C_2H_5COOH}$** (propanoic acid).
- **C** ($\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$, the alkanes): $\mathrm{CH_4}$, $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$, then **$\mathrm{C_3H_8}$** (propane) is the third member.

(Note: the first carboxylic acid is methanoic acid, $\mathrm{HCOOH}$, which fits the formula with $n = 0$. If a marker counts B from $n = 1$, the third member would be $\mathrm{C_3H_7COOH}$, butanoic acid.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the reagent and the reaction condition for the conversion of A to C.

Reagent: ...

Condition: ... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A (an alkene) is converted to C (the alkane) by **hydrogenation** (addition of hydrogen across the double bond).

- **Reagent:** hydrogen gas, $\mathrm{H_2}$.
- **Condition:** a **nickel catalyst** at about $150\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

For example $\mathrm{C_2H_4} + \mathrm{H_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_6}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Name the type of reaction that occurs in the conversion of D to B. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Oxidation.** An alcohol (D) is oxidised to the carboxylic acid (B), for example with acidified potassium dichromate(VI) or acidified potassium manganate(VII), or by the action of air and bacteria (ethanol to ethanoic acid).

questions.enonce_markdown:
The second member of B reacts with the third member of D to produce a compound.

(i) Name the compound.

(ii) How can you easily identify this compound?

(iii) Identify the catalyst for this reaction. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The second member of B (counting from methanoic acid, $\mathrm{HCOOH}$) is ethanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$. The third member of D is propan-1-ol, $\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}$ ($\mathrm{CH_3OH}$, $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}$, $\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}$).

$\mathrm{CH_3COOH} + \mathrm{C_3H_7OH} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CH_3COOC_3H_7} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

(i) The compound is an ester: **propyl ethanoate** (esterification).

(ii) By its **sweet, fruity smell** (esters have pleasant fruity odours).

(iii) The catalyst is **concentrated sulphuric acid** (a few drops, with warming).

(If B were counted from $n = 1$, its second member would be propanoic acid and the ester propyl propanoate, $\mathrm{C_2H_5COOC_3H_7}$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Give a reagent that can be used to distinguish between A and C. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Bromine water** (or acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution). Add it to each hydrocarbon: the alkene A **decolourises** the orange-brown bromine water (it is unsaturated and adds bromine across the double bond), while the alkane C leaves it unchanged (orange-brown).
